title: Proposed reworking of 'About:' info
description:
**This is just one possible presentation of the information.** Suggestions for other possible presentations are welcome on #17960.

Make the information in `tshark -v` output and Wireshark's "About"
dialog easier to read, by presenting present/absent dependencies in
columns (similar to UNIX `ls`) instead of as a run-on sentence.

The `+`/`-` prefix is kept to allow the test harness to be able to tell
whether a feature is present or not. Alternately, the test harness could
be made to look for features between a 'With:' and a (possibly not
present) 'Without:' in the output to determine their presence.

Closes #17960

notes.body:
This format is better for a bug report printout, definitely more readable, but worse for an "About" dialog or version information.

I think the best solution is to remove the compile/runtime information from "--version" and adding a new flag to generate the extra verbose report (for the CLI).

... or add an `--porcelain` flag to it. 
- Without it (so by default) you get the human readable output.
- With it you get machine readable output

gitlab@mg.gitlab.com>:

`g_string_replace` was introduced in [GLib 2.68](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/method.String.replace.html), which is higher than our current minimum (and later than what's included with RHEL 8, Debian Bullseye, some other distributions).

We could add an implementation to wsutil/glib-compat.h, or do something else on versions with older GLib (just not replace the string, even?)
The reason for removing it is to shorten the string to fit 3 columns to reduce scrolling as that was one concern.
Hmm, only used on Windows realy. Move it to where the npcap version string is added?

> Hmm, only used on Windows realy.

No, the result of `pcap_get_lib_version()` on UN\*Xes and [Haiku](https://www.haiku-os.org) also includes the word "version". (Yes, [Wireshark has been ported to Haiku](https://depot.haiku-os.org/#!/pkg/wireshark/haikuports/haikuports_x86_64/4/0/5/-/1/x86_64?bcguid=bc2-PAQE).)

> Move it to where the npcap version string is added?

No, leave it there.
